The three recurring onboarding blockers appearing consistently across the implementation data logs and the playbook are:

1. **Permission Mapping**: This is the most common blocker, accounting for 45% of delay incidents in implementation logs [NL-031#NL-031-S04] and 45% of onboarding delays in Q2 data [NL-012#NL-012-S06]. The playbook also confirms it is the most common blocker for Enterprise accounts [NL-005#NL-005-S06]. A technical root cause is that the permission worker sync script encounters recursion limits on nested group configurations with circular dependencies, halting directory mirroring [NL-031#NL-031-S04].

2. **Source Ingestion Cleanup**: This accounts for 30% of delay incidents [NL-031#NL-031-S04] and 30% of onboarding delays [NL-012#NL-012-S06]. Customers dump unreviewed folders into KnowledgeHub, resulting in outdated policy versions, requiring a manual document audit and cleanup to purge duplicate and stale files [NL-031#NL-031-S04].

3. **OCR and Scanned PDFs**: This accounts for 25% of delay incidents [NL-031#NL-031-S04] and 25% of onboarding delays [NL-012#NL-012-S06]. The standard PDF parser fails to detect text layers in image-only documents, resulting in empty indexes and incomplete citations that fail the go-live validation threshold unless external OCR pre-processing is applied [NL-031#NL-031-S04]. This was the primary blocker for BrightPath Healthcare's 9.5-week onboarding [NL-031#NL-031-S04][NL-012#NL-012-S06].

The playbook's remediation path also categorizes failure causes into similar buckets—extraction errors, semantic mapping gaps, or conflicting source policies—which map to these three blockers [NL-005#NL-005-S11].
